bands.1:
You have won Narra the Teller's badge. Now he is on your side.

"The tide goes out at midnight," says Narra. "It comes back in 45 minutes. Then the cave is the sea's story."

"Story," squeaks Echobat, his tiny bat. "Story."

Indi's disguises are big headphones made of coconuts. Mo's coconut still has milk in it. It drips down his neck.

Gus holds up a bottle. "The Burp Bottle! Three weeks of my best burps."

At midnight, you splash along the sandbar to the cave. Two Goldies guard the gold door. They wear big headphones.

Gus opens the bottle next to their microphones. BRRRAAAP! The Goldies stumble away, dizzy.

Zed types MAXXSOUNDSAMAZING. The door opens.

Inside is the Echo Studio. It is padded with gold foam. Cages line the wall. There are Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings and a Murkle.

On the desk are tapes. Each one says, "HAPPY NOISES (ME)."

Zed plays one. First you hear hatchlings crying. Then you hear Maxx in a squeaky voice. "Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero!"

"Nailed it," says the real Maxx. "That's Maxx-imum content."

"That is not the hatchlings' story," says Narra. "That is his."

You put the tapes in your bag. That is the proof.

Wren opens the cages. Then water rushes over the floor. The tide is coming back! The Goldies are coming back too.

Echobat flies out. It shouts in Maxx's voice, "Goldies! Back to the yacht!"

The Goldies run off.

You splash back with hatchlings in every pocket. On the beach, the Dashlings race into the sea.

On the boat, Zed plays one last tape. It is a deep, slow song from far out at sea. The label says, "THE BIG ONE. Play this to bring her close. Bring the biggest net."

It is the song of Old Glimmer, the giant glowing ray. Narra listens with his eyes shut.

"She is singing to someone," he whispers. "Someone small."
bands.2:
Now that you have his badge, Narra the Teller tells you something useful.

"The tide goes out at midnight," he says, "and comes back at quarter to one. That is the crew's story, Captain. Forty-five minutes. After that, it is the sea's story."

"Story," squeaks Echobat from his hat. "Story."

"That's a fifty-fifty chance of a flooded cave," says Tully. "Still better odds than the Reef Rays."

Indi's disguises are sound engineers, with giant headphones made from coconut halves. Mo's coconut still has milk in it, and it dribbles down his neck whenever he nods.

Gus holds up a corked bottle. "The Burp Bottle," he whispers. "Three weeks of my finest burps."

At midnight, the sandbar rises out of the lagoon like a road. You splash along it to the cave. Two Goldies sit by the gold door, wearing enormous headphones.

Gus uncorks the bottle right beside their microphones. BRRRAAAAAP! The Goldies rip off their headphones and stagger out onto the sand, too dizzy to stand.

Zed types MAXXSOUNDSAMAZING, and the door clicks open. "Speedrun," he grins.

The Echo Studio is padded with gold foam. There's a desk covered in sliders and a glass booth with a gold microphone. Cages line the back wall: Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings and a sulky Murkle hiding in its own ink.

On the desk is a stack of tapes. Every label says, "HAPPY NOISES (ME)."

Zed plays one. First comes the real sound: hatchlings squealing in fright. Then, on top, comes Maxx in a squeaky voice. "Squee! Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero!"

Then, in his normal voice: "Nailed it. That's Maxx-imum content."

"That is not the hatchlings' story," Narra says softly. "That is his."

"His," says Echobat. "His."

You pack the tapes into your waterproof bag. That's the proof.

Wren opens the cages. Then water swirls across the floor. The tide is coming back early, and so are the Goldies.

Echobat has heard Maxx so often that it can copy his voice perfectly. It flies out over the Goldies and shouts, "Goldies! Back to the yacht, now!"

The Goldies salute and run.

You splash back along the sinking sandbar, with hatchlings in every pocket. On the beach, the Dashlings race for the sea, and this time nothing stops them.

Back on the boat, Zed plays the last tape. It's a deep, slow, beautiful song, recorded far out at sea. The label says, "THE BIG ONE. Play this to lure her close. Bring the biggest net."

It is the song of Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray. Narra listens with his eyes shut.

"Narra the Teller hears something else in it," he whispers. "She is singing to someone. Someone small."
bands.3:
You have won Narra the Teller's badge, so at last Narra the Teller tells you something useful.

"The tide goes out at midnight," he says, "and comes back at quarter to one. That is the crew's story, Captain. Forty-five minutes to get in and get out. After that, it becomes the sea's story."

"Story," squeaks Echobat from his hat. "Story."

"That's a fifty-fifty chance of being trapped in a flooded cave," says Tully. "Which is still better than the Reef Rays' chance of making the finals."

Indi's disguises are sound engineers: giant headphones made from coconut halves, and a clipboard each. Mo's coconut still has milk in it, which dribbles down his neck every time he nods.

Gus has his gadget in a corked bottle. "The Burp Bottle," he whispers. "Three weeks of my finest burps, squashed in tight. That's not gross. That's science."

At midnight, the sandbar rises out of the lagoon like a road. You splash along it to the cave, where two Goldies sit by the gold door wearing enormous headphones, nodding to music.

Gus creeps up behind them and uncorks the Burp Bottle right beside their microphones.

BRRRAAAAAAP.

The burp is so loud and so long that the Goldies rip off their headphones and stagger out onto the sandbar, too dizzy to see straight.

Zed types MAXXSOUNDSAMAZING into the keypad, and the door clicks open. "Speedrun," he grins.

The Echo Studio is padded from floor to ceiling with gold foam. There's a mixing desk covered in sliders and a glass booth with a single gold microphone. Along the back wall are cages: Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings, a sulky Murkle hiding in its own ink cloud and a Sidlewink clicking nervously.

On the desk is a stack of tapes. Every label says the same thing, in gold pen: "HAPPY NOISES (ME)."

Zed slides one into the machine. First comes the real sound, recorded on the beach: hatchlings squealing in fright. Then a second track begins on top. It's Maxx, alone in the booth, in a high, squeaky voice. "Squee! Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero, Maxx!"

Then, in his normal voice: "Nailed it. That's Maxx-imum content."

"That is not the hatchlings' story," Narra says softly. "That is his."

"His," says Echobat. "His."

You pack the tapes into your waterproof bag. That's the proof.

Wren and Narra open the cages. The Dashlings head straight for the door. The Duettles argue about who should go first, until Wren picks them both up at once.

Then water swirls across the floor. The tide is coming back early, and outside, the Goldies are splashing back along the sandbar.

Echobat has heard Maxx so often in this cave that it can copy his voice perfectly. It flutters out over the Goldies and shouts, "Goldies! Back to the yacht, now! Smash that heart button!"

The Goldies salute and race off.

You splash back along the sinking sandbar, waist-deep, with hatchlings tucked into every pocket. On the beach, the Dashlings sprint for the water, and this time nothing stops them.

Back on the boat, Zed plays the last tape in the pile. It isn't happy noises. It's the deep, slow, beautiful song of something enormous, recorded far out at sea. The label says, "THE BIG ONE. Play this to lure her close. Bring the biggest net."

It is the song of Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray from the old sea stories. Narra the Teller listens with his eyes shut, and for once Echobat does not repeat a thing.

"Narra the Teller hears what Maxx did not," he whispers at last. "She is singing to someone. Someone small."
bands.4:
Now that his badge is pinned to your jacket, Narra the Teller finally tells you something useful.

"The tide goes out at midnight," he says, "and comes back at quarter to one. That is the crew's story, Captain: forty-five minutes to get in and out. After that, it becomes the sea's story."

"Story," squeaks Echobat from the brim of his hat. "Story."

"That's a fifty-fifty chance of being trapped in a flooded cave," says Tully, "which is still better than the Reef Rays' chance of making the finals."

Indi has turned everyone into sound engineers, with giant headphones made from coconut halves and a clipboard each for looking busy. Mo's coconut still has milk in it, and every time he nods, a little more dribbles down the back of his neck.

At midnight, the sandbar rises out of the lagoon like a road. At the far end, beside the gold padded door, two Goldies sit in enormous headphones, nodding along to music only they can hear.

Gus creeps up behind them, uncorks a bottle holding three weeks of his own burps, and holds it right against their microphones.

BRRRAAAAAAAP.

Ripping off their headphones, the Goldies stagger out onto the sand, too dizzy to tell the cave from the sea. Zed types MAXXSOUNDSAMAZING, and the door clicks open before either of them can turn round.

The Echo Studio is padded from floor to ceiling in gold foam, so that your footsteps, your breathing and even your heartbeat seem to vanish into it. There is a mixing desk covered in sliders, and a glass booth with a single gold microphone. Along the back wall, in tanks and cages, are the island's missing Creatures: Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings, a sulky Murkle hiding in its own cloud of ink, and a Sidlewink clicking nervously at the dark.

On the desk sits a stack of tapes, each labelled in gold pen: "HAPPY NOISES (ME)."

Zed slides one into the machine. First comes the beach, and under the waves, hatchlings squealing in a way no one could mistake for happy. Then a second track begins on top of it: Maxx, alone in the booth, in a high, squeaky voice. "Squee! Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero, Maxx! Squeeeee!"

There is a pause on the tape, and then his normal voice. "Nailed it."

Narra takes off his straw hat and holds it against his chest, the way people do at a funeral. "That is not the hatchlings' story," he says. "That is his."

"His," says Echobat. "His."

You slide the tapes into your waterproof bag while Wren and Narra open the cages. The Dashlings make straight for the door, because a Dashling only ever wants one thing, and it is not a gold foam room. The Duettles argue about who should go first, and who is rescuing whom, until Wren picks them both up at once.

Then a thin sheet of water slides across the floor.

It is only half past twelve. Tully looks at her watch, then at the water, and for once she does not give anyone the odds. Outside, the Goldies have found their feet and are splashing back along a sandbar that is getting narrower by the second.

Echobat has hung in this cave through a hundred of Maxx's recording nights. It knows every word, and every way he says it. Fluttering out over the Goldies' heads, it shouts in a voice that is not its own: "Goldies! Back to the yacht, now! Smash that heart button!"

The Goldies salute and run.

You wade back waist-deep, with hatchlings tucked into every pocket, while behind you the cave mouth slips quietly under the waves. On the beach, the Dashlings sprint for the water, and this time nothing stops them.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, Zed plays the last tape in the pile, just to check. It is not happy noises. It is a song, deep and slow and enormous, recorded somewhere far out at sea. On the label, Maxx has written: "THE BIG ONE. Play this to lure her close. Bring the biggest net."

It is the song of Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray of the old sea stories. Narra the Teller listens with his eyes shut, all the way to the end, and Echobat, for once, repeats nothing.

"Maxx heard a song he could use," Narra says at last. "Narra the Teller hears something else." He opens his eyes. "She is singing to someone. Someone small."
